Summary:
The MOVEit Transfer vulnerability CVE-2023-34362 is a remote code execution (RCE) flaw in the MOVEit Transfer software, which allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the affected system.

Why it matters:
This vulnerability was exploited by attackers to steal sensitive data from various organizations. The exploitation of this vulnerability highlights the importance of timely patching and secure configuration of critical systems.

Recommended actions / Mitigations:
Apply the patches provided by Progress Software, the vendor of MOVEit Transfer, as soon as possible. Ensure that all systems are running the latest version of the software. Implement a robust security information and event management (SIEM) system to detect potential exploitation attempts. Conduct thorough risk assessments and implement additional security controls as necessary.

Evidence:
The vulnerability was publicly disclosed on April 26, 2023, by Progress Software. The company released patches for the vulnerability shortly after disclosure. Multiple reports of exploitation have been documented in the wild, indicating that attackers are actively targeting this vulnerability.

Unknowns / Gaps:
It is unclear how many organizations have been affected by this vulnerability and whether any specific actor groups are responsible for the exploitation attempts.
